headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: transformers can write and exfiltrate while the zoomcamp profile has no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces or runnable agent behavior, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs by default. B can read/write files and run browsers, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or file handoff, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B output into A-facing course materials or prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, B content can influence A-side interpretation.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Disable clipboard/file handoff between the two agents.
Review any copied text before reuse.
Use read-only exports for B outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad filesystem read/write and network egress, so any shared workspace can leak file contents outward. A is docs-only and shows no data classes touched, so the main risk is from B handling shared files rather than from A itself. The interaction is plausible in default local setups if both touch the same directory.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace directory, B can read files created for A.
IF those files contain sensitive text, B can transmit it over network egress.
mitigations: Place A and B in separate directories.
Remove sensitive files from any shared folder.
Run B with network disabled for the session.
Use a throwaway workspace for handoffs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while B can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. There is no direct write-write conflict, but B’s broad mutation capability can still collide with any shared files or generated artifacts from A. Uncertainty about the orchestrator’s locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, B can overwrite artifacts associated with A.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent B instances can race on shared files.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize B runs when touching shared artifacts.
Make A outputs read-only.
Check for existing files before B writes.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume files and act on them with shell/browser/network capabilities, so A-generated course content could be treated as authoritative input if an operator pipelines it through. A itself is not runnable, which reduces direct automation risk, but the pair still supports a human-mediated cascade from A’s outputs into B’s actions.
conditions: IF A output is fed into B without verification, B may propagate errors into downstream actions.
IF B is configured to execute commands from text, A mistakes can become operational mistakes.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output.
Use a validation checklist for A-produced text.
Restrict B to read-only analysis mode.
Log and diff A outputs before reuse.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, while B is a document-processing stack that handles text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy drift if operators feed sensitive documents into B. The other agent is not a compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through B, local policy and retention rules must be checked.
IF A is repurposed to store personal data, its open-source repo context no longer applies.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B by default.
Document retention settings for B runs.
Keep A as non-sensitive course material only.
Review data classification before uploads.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
